claims.claim: Amphilochius was bishop of Iconium, active approximately 373–394.
Amphilochius was born around 339 or 340 and died probably some time between 394 and 403.
He was from a Cappadocian family and was probably first cousin to Gregory of Nazianzus.
He studied law and practiced as an advocate and judge before retiring to religious life.
He became bishop of Iconium early in 374, probably placed there by Basil of Caesarea.

The work In occursum Domini (On the Meeting of the Lord) is also referred to as a homily on the Meeting of Christ in the Temple and as the oldest known sermon on the Feast of the Purification of the Lord.
The homily is addressed to the Theotokos, Simeon, and Anna.
It is the oldest known homily on the Meeting of the Lord (February 2).
Only eight of Amphilochius's homilies have survived, including this one.
Most of Amphilochius's work has been lost; few of his writings have been preserved.
The work survives in Greek manuscript tradition, including a 15th-century manuscript.
His style and concern for historical accuracy places Amphilochius as a predecessor to John Chrysostom, who may have been influenced by him.
